long_biography.plain_text:
Austal founder John Rothwell began his career in practical trades. After leaving school at fifteen, he worked in welding and steel fabrication before establishing a small engineering company. That business became the base for Star Boats, whose aluminium hulls found customers among Australian crayfish fishermen.

When Rothwell launched Austal with former colleagues, winning an overseas order did not immediately solve its financing problem. The first Chinese customer required a bank guarantee that the young company lacked the security to provide. After other banks refused, Standard Chartered backed the contract and then a second order. Rothwell later chose outside investors partly for their business skills and contacts, while keeping management simple and giving staff responsibility.
long_biography.html:
Austal founder John Rothwell began his career in practical trades. After leaving school at fifteen, he worked in welding and steel fabrication before establishing a small engineering company. That business became the base for Star Boats, whose aluminium hulls found customers among Australian crayfish fishermen.

When Rothwell launched Austal with former colleagues, winning an overseas order did not immediately solve its financing problem. The first Chinese customer required a bank guarantee that the young company lacked the security to provide. After other banks refused, Standard Chartered backed the contract and then a second order. Rothwell later chose outside investors partly for their business skills and contacts, while keeping management simple and giving staff responsibility.
